text:
Education in Greece features a compulsory system lasting nine years, comprising six years of primary school (Dimotiko) and three years of lower secondary school (Gymnasium), followed by three years of non-compulsory upper secondary education (Lyceum). The school year typically runs from September 11 to June 15. Primary education includes a two-year compulsory preschool stage (Pre-kindergarten and Kindergarten) for children aged 4–6, where students begin learning English. Grading in primary school starts in the third year with letters (A–C), shifts to numbers (1–10) in the fifth year, and includes written exams in the sixth year. Upon completion, students receive an automatic admission certificate to the Gymnasium.
Secondary education is divided into the Gymnasium (ages 12–15) and the Lyceum (ages 15–18). The Gymnasium is compulsory, offering various types such as Special, Model, Experimental, and Vocational schools, with English mandatory throughout. Students choose a second foreign language (French or German) in the third year. Admission to the non-compulsory Lyceum requires a Gymnasium certificate; students aged 15 to 20 can apply, with Evening Lyceums available for adults and working students. The Lyceum uses a 1–20 grading system and offers General High Schools (Geniko Lykeio) where students select one of three orientation groups in their final year: Humanities, Science and Health, or Economic and Computer Studies. Admission to higher education requires the Lyceum certificate and passing the Pan-Hellenic Examinations, a national standardized test. Vocational pathways include the Vocational Lyceum (EPAL), which combines academic and technical training in specialized streams, and apprenticeship programs like EPAS and Post-lyceum Year Apprenticeship Class that integrate workplace training.
Higher education is provided by public and private Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). Public universities offer tuition-free or low-cost education for most students, with some programs available in English. Admission to university requires the Lyceum certificate and successful completion of the Pan-Hellenic Examinations, which determine admission based on weighted exam scores, high school GPAs, and university preferences. The system also includes specialized institutions such as the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme, starting in 2026, and various vocational training schools for adults and those seeking specialized skills. Non-formal education options include open online courses and digital academies managed by the Ministry of Education and academic networks.
